Last week, Apple filed a lawsuit against OpenAI, alleging that its former employee "stole trade secrets for OpenAI's benefit."

As part of the lawsuit proceedings, Apple has reportedly sent letters directly to dozens of former employees now working at OpenAI.

According to the Financial Times, Apple has issued legal preservation notices to approximately 40 former employees.

A preservation notice is a formal written notice sent to an individual or organization requiring them to preserve documents, records and other evidence that may be relevant to a legal dispute. Such notices typically specify what exactly should be preserved.

The move comes as Apple suspects that the alleged trade secret theft may not be limited to those named in last week's initial lawsuit.

Notably, Apple's lawsuit names OpenAI and io Products as defendants, along with former Apple employees Chang Liu and Tang Tan.
